mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) during the specified FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) by at least 50,000 jobs predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS increase is not met.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1500 units in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to stronger consumer demand momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying demand periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 5% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary conditions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines as specified.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and stronger equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the unemployment decline period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 2% predict a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as stronger aggregate demand supports equity performance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above their 2023 Q4 averages produces a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to conflicting effects of higher rates and weaker labor market (interaction effect).
regime_hint: Dual pressure: higher rates and rising unemployment
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both proxies are above their historical thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: During a 'late-cycle expansion' regime (as defined by CPIAUCSL > 208 and PAYEMS > 140,000), the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to momentum from strong inflation and employment signals.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in the specified regime.
